prompt: Before letting the agent edit files, you ask it to propose which files it will change and how, and you approve it.
tells: propose which files it will change and how
why: Review the plan before code; redirecting a plan is cheaper than redoing code.
trap: The spec was already there; this is the how.

prompt: The agent implemented caching inside every controller instead of in the shared data layer, and you only noticed in a 2,000-line diff.
why: A short plan review would have caught the wrong approach before any code.
trap: Smaller tasks help, but the approach itself was wrong.

prompt: A database migration could lock large tables. You want the agent to explain its approach, risks and rollback before writing it.
tells: explain its approach, risks and rollback
why: Plan first, especially for risky changes.
trap: Criteria say what; the plan says how and what could go wrong.

prompt: For an unfamiliar codebase, the agent first reads relevant code and writes up a plan, then a fresh session implements it.
why: Research → plan → implement, with the plan as the hand-off.
trap: Separating phases keeps each one focused.
